summary: Independently re-derived, from source and fresh adversarial probes, whether Phase 134B.1's external-notification isolation repair held at a channel-agnostic architectural boundary rather than trusting its report. Found BLOCKING: isolation was a five-name environment-variable deny-list plus one call site's (finalize_phase_report) master-switch check, while a second real dispatch call site (pcae notify send-report) bypassed that switch entirely, constructing TelegramSink() directly and gated only by that one adapter's own env check. Proved the gap with a fresh reproducible test. Repaired minimally by adding one fail-closed, transport-independent authorization gate inside pcae.core.notifications.dispatch() -- the shared function every call site (current and future) already uses -- keyed on an explicit local/no-network sink allowlist rather than a per-channel name list, so future adapters inherit protection automatically. Production notification behavior, PFN-001, and exactly-once logical completion preserved except that pcae notify send-report now also requires PCAE_NOTIFY_ENABLED=1 (already set in the operator's real environment).
